payload.pattern: A gate that cannot fail: an aggregator deriving health from child-process exit codes cannot distinguish a clean gate from one that found a violation but was not asked to care, or from one with no failure condition at all.
payload.solution: Census every gate in the roster for FIRABILITY UNDER THE ARGV THE AGGREGATOR PASSES. Verdicts: FIRABLE / NO-FAILURE-CONDITION / UNFIRABLE-AS-INVOKED / DISCLOSED-ALTERNATE-CHANNEL / DEGRADED. Track unfalsifiableWeight = registered score weight that cannot move. Precision-first: only call a gate unfirable when the blocking flag is a top-level conjunct; a || or ! or an unresolvable expression is DEGRADED, never a conviction. Both directions: an undeclared unfirable gate is a hard finding, and a disclosure declaration left on a gate that IS firable is reported STALE. Obelisk found a weight-20 gate that was an inventory printer with no exit statement (20/20 every run for ~190 sessions) and two gates printing red findings while the doctor recorded ok. Fixing the gates was not enough: the aggregator excluded warn from every tally, so a weightless gate exiting 1 reached no field at all. Reference: obelisk scripts/lib/gate-firability.mjs + scripts/check-gate-firability.mjs (W231).

payload.headline: A gate exit code answers how it was called, not what it found — unfalsifiableWeight 20/110 to 0/110.
payload.notableForSiblings: If your repo has a health command that fans out to child processes and aggregates their exit codes, it very likely has at least one gate that cannot fail. Obelisk found three, plus a canonical source-stripper with no regex-literal state that had been silently blanking the tails of 17 of 691 files inside two security gates perimeters.
